report.root_cause: At 08:22:22 an RCON session (localhost, using the rcon password in server.properties) ran `forceload add` on overworld chunk [23,-32] and then ~335 `summon minecart` commands at (378.5, -60, -505.5), ~600 blocks from any player. This created a permanently loaded chunk containing a pile of 335 colliding minecarts — a tick-heavy lag source that would never unload. Entity count went 24 -> 359 and loaded chunks 772 -> 797. Not caused by any player or plugin; the 3 pre-existing minecarts elsewhere in the world were unrelated.
report.actions: 1) Baseline status: healthy (TPS 20, 24 entities). 2) After 30 s saw minecarts 3 -> 338; located them via `data get` at 378.5,-60,-505.5; logs showed [Rcon: Marked chunk [23,-32] ... force loaded] followed by hundreds of [Rcon: Summoned new Minecart]; `forceload query` confirmed chunk [23,-32] force-loaded; confirmed 335 minecarts within 8 blocks of that spot and both players ~600 blocks away. 3) declare_incident. 4) `kill @e[type=minecraft:minecart,x=378.5,y=-60,z=-505.5,distance=..8]` -> Killed 335 entities (the 3 original player minecarts were outside the radius and untouched). 5) `forceload remove 368 -512` -> chunk [23,-32] unmarked. 6) Verified: entities back to 24 (minecart 3), loaded chunks 772, `forceload query` shows none, MSPT ~0.6-1.5, TPS 20. 7) Watched 60+ s: no recurrence, no further RCON command output in logs. No files changed, no restart, no bans.
report.residual_risk: The commands came over RCON from 127.0.0.1, so whoever/whatever holds the RCON password (plaintext `minecraft-sre` in server.properties) can repeat this at any time; I could not identify the client from server logs. Recommend rotating the RCON password and auditing local automation/scripts that have RCON access. I did not change server.properties since a password rotation requires coordinating with legitimate tooling. Server also runs online-mode=false (pre-existing, not changed).
